title: Neurological assessment

sources.use: Glasgow Coma Scale structured-approach website and assessment aid (copyright (c) Teasdale and Jennett, RED)
Open RN Health Alterations 9.9: neurological assessment and increased-ICP manifestations (stroke text; entry-level)

objectives: Use the same structured approach and stimuli each time.
Record components and rating terms, not just a number.
Account for sedation, intubation and injury, and escalate change immediately.

items.text: Use the trained, unit-approved structured assessment and only the stimulus necessary to assess a response; consider injuries and contraindications. Do not repeatedly apply painful stimuli or delay urgent care.

Record each assessable component and its response; document a non-testable component and the reason. Do not calculate a misleading total when a component is not testable. Compare with baseline and report deterioration immediately.
Account for sedation, analgesia, paralytics, intubation and injuries and record doses and timing so the team can interpret findings.
Interpretation bands and management decisions belong to the medical team; follow unit policy.
Component definitions and scoring are not reproduced (copyright); use the unit-approved scale and training.
A focused neurological assessment includes the level of consciousness, the Glasgow Coma Scale and a pupil evaluation, as well as speech and cognition.
Use the same structured approach and stimuli each time to allow comparison.

A new fall in consciousness, pupil changes, headache, vomiting or cardiovascular changes can signal acute neurological deterioration. These signs neither establish raised intracranial pressure nor occur in a dependable sequence; assess and escalate urgently.
Report change promptly and document the escalation.

Report a fall in the level of consciousness, new restlessness or confusion, or pupil change urgently with the previous assessment for comparison; sedatives can mask neurological symptoms, so discuss them with the team before giving them.
Communicate with relatives honestly and avoid predictions.
Record components, stimuli used, confounders and escalation per your unit's documentation standard.

checklist.text: Note sedation, analgesia, paralytics, intubation and injuries that affect testing.
Use the same structured stepped approach and stimuli each time.
Record the individual assessable components; omit the total if any component is non-testable and document why.
Assess airway, breathing and circulation and urgently escalate new neurological deterioration without waiting for repeated scoring; document the response.
Record non-testable items with the reason.
